newsitem.title: UK: UK opposition withdraws cooperation in parliament.
newsitem.headline: UK opposition withdraws cooperation in parliament.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour and Liberal Democrat parties said on Tuesday they would end cooperation with the ruling Conservatives from January after what they said was government "double counting" in a key vote.

The decision will make it harder for Prime Minister John Major to pass legislation and thus continue in power until the latest date for an election ain May. The government, lagging in polls, last week lost its parliamentary majority.

Labour parliamentary business manager Donald Dewar and Archie Kirkwood of the Liberal Democrats told a joint news conference they had discovered the double counting after the government survived a key vote on Europe on Monday by 11 votes.

Dewar said they found that the government had offered both parties the same three names of members of parliament for "pairing" -- a system to allow MPs to be absent for key votes without affecting the overall result.

"Prima facie, this is cheating and it's never happened before," said Kirkwood, who said he expected most other smaller opposition parties to follow suit. Dewar and Kirkwood raised the matter with the Conservatives, who are investigating.

Dewar said: "We have in all the circumstances decided ...there will be no pairing arrangements from the return of the House in January." This means the government can be ambushed at any minute, making life increasingly difficult for its MPs.
